title: SCM drift canary: compare estimate vs metered attribution on fixed prompt set
author: Rafael Mendes
description: Motivation: We’ve had a few reports (SUP-8821, INT-1058) where Console/Optimize surfaced cost deltas that didn’t line up with what the runtime telemetry implied, especially when batching/caching changed. This PR adds a lightweight canary job in perf-canary that continuously compares SCM /estimate outputs against metered attribution derived from runtime+telemetry for a fixed prompt set. The goal is to catch drift early (kernel changes, telemetry tag regressions, batch_size_effective bugs, SKU metadata changes, etc.) and alert with enough context to debug quickly. What this adds: (1) A new canary suite `scm_drift` that runs every 10 minutes in each canary region (initially: us-east-1, eu-west-1) against staging and prod-canary endpoints. The suite replays a fixed prompt set (curated for prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, and mixed; includes a couple of longer context cases to exercise KV cache behavior). (2) For each prompt case, we call Cost Model API v1 `/estimate` with explicit inputs (model_id, quant_profile_id, region, gpu_sku, expected_tokens, and scenario flags), then fetch metered attribution for the same request from telemetry (token metering + SCM-aligned dimensions). We compute drift metrics: absolute delta ($), relative delta (%), and component drift for compute/memory/cache if present. (3) Export metrics to Prometheus: `scm_drift_ratio`, `scm_drift_abs_usd`, `scm_drift_component_ratio{component=...}`, plus bookkeeping series for missing telemetry dimensions. (4) Alerting: fires when p95 drift ratio > 1.15 (15%) for 3 consecutive runs OR when `missing_dimension_rate` > 0.02 (2%) for 2 consecutive runs. Alerts are routed to #eng-sre + #eng-platform with a runbook link and a sampled breakdown (sanitized) of the worst offenders. (5) Guardrails: uses a synthetic tenant + a dedicated API key scoped to canary. Payloads are non-customer prompts (internal text), and request IDs are tagged with `canary_suite=scm_drift` to make it easy to filter in logs/metrics. The job will not page on a single outlier; it requires consecutive failures and includes a 'telemetry lag' suppression window (see `--max-telemetry-lag-seconds`, default 180s). (6) Versioning: canary requests explicitly set `X-Redwood-Cost-Model-Version: 1` and also emits `requested_version`/`resolved_version` as labels, so we can detect unexpected negotiation behavior. Notes / limitations: Metered attribution is derived from telemetry and is subject to lag and partial ingestion; the job waits up to `maxTelemetryLag` for the attribution record to materialize, then records a 'missing_attribution' metric if still absent. This is intended to detect regressions in metering and tagging as well. Follow-ups: once SCM v2 lands, we should extend this suite to run both v1 and v2 in parallel and compare them (without alerting) for 1-2 weeks before switching thresholds. Related work: redwood PRs implementing SCM service + explain endpoint, and the recent batch_size_effective regression fix. See also the SLO dashboards work; this canary is intended as a higher-level correctness signal that complements latency/error checks.
commits: canary/scm_drift: add fixed prompt set + scenario matrix
canary/scm_drift: implement Cost Model API client (version-pinned) and request tagging
canary/scm_drift: implement telemetry lookup + drift computation (ratio/abs/component)
metrics: export drift + missing dimension metrics to prometheus
alerts: add scm_drift alert rules + runbook link
docs: add canary suite README and oncall troubleshooting steps
ci: wire scm_drift suite into scheduled canary workflow
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): Thresholds look reasonable, but can we avoid noisy alerts from telemetry lag? Also please make sure we never page on staging drift. Rafael Mendes (author): Added `--max-telemetry-lag-seconds` (default 180s) and a separate metric `scm_drift_missing_attribution_total`. Alerting now requires consecutive failures and is only enabled for prod-canary environments. Staging runs are recorded but no alert rules apply. Logan Wright (Telemetry): Please add explicit counters for missing required SCM dimensions (region, gpu_sku, quant_profile_id) so we can distinguish 'no record' vs 'bad tags'. Rafael Mendes: Done. Added `scm_drift_missing_dimension_total{dimension=...}` and the alert includes the top missing dimensions in annotations. Jordan Lee (Versioning/determinism): Ensure request includes SCM version header and record negotiated version. Also don’t fail hard if server returns 406/unsupported version; track it as a separate metric. Rafael Mendes: Added `X-Redwood-Cost-Model-Version: 1` and label `resolved_version`. Unsupported version increments `scm_drift_version_unsupported_total` and marks the run as failed only if it persists 3 runs (to avoid transient deploy rollouts). Marissa Cole (Console): Can we include a human-readable breakdown snippet in the alert so support/oncall can answer 'why did it drift'? Rafael Mendes: Alert now includes (sanitized) worst-case prompt_case + model_id + component ratios and the top two assumptions from the estimate response. Also linked the runbook section 'How to interpret component drift'. Approvals: Sean Gallagher approved; Logan Wright approved; Jordan Lee approved; Marissa Cole approved.
